subject: Residency & customer-controlled storage: operations and deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@helioshealth.com>

Cc: Helios Security <security@helioshealth.com>

Subject: Residency & customer-controlled storage: operations questions

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this — we're finalizing our Private/VPC evaluation and have a couple of operational questions we need to close with procurement and InfoSec. Can you confirm the following for Redwood Private (VPC + customer-controlled storage):

- Confirmation that customer data can be stored on customer-managed volumes in our VPC (we want to ensure we control the snapshots and lifecycle).
- Snapshot & backup retention: how are snapshots retained, how long before automatic purge, and can we request immediate deletion of specific snapshots?
- Wipe & evidence: when a tenant requests a full erase, what evidence/logs do you produce (audit trails, deletion certificates)? Procurement wants a sample of the deletion evidence that we could hand to our auditors.
- KMS: can we bring our own KMS keys (BYOK) and ensure keys are under our control so data becomes inaccessible after key destruction?
- Timeline: how long does a full sanitization process take (logical delete -> physical wipe -> attestation)?

If there's a short playbook or one-pager you can share that outlines the operational steps we would execute together (and what Redwood does vs. what Helios needs to do), that would be super helpful.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Monroe
Head of Cloud Security
Helios Health

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency & customer-controlled storage: operations questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I've attached a short ops playbook that walks through the steps. Marissa (cc'd) will own producing the sample artifacts you requested.

High-level: Redwood Private supports customer-controlled storage in two deployment patterns:

1) Customer-managed volumes in their cloud account (we run a small control plane with no tenant data persisted outside the VPC).
2) Customer-storage within Redwood-managed infra but encrypted with customer-supplied KMS (BYOK).

Snapshots & retention:
- Snapshots are tenant-scoped and retained per a TTL configured at onboarding. Default TTL is 30 days; we can change per-customer.
- Immediate snapshot delete: we support an administrative "expunge" operation for a specified snapshot id. That triggers logical deletion and the snapshot is queued for garbage collection and physical zeroing on the next scrub cycle.

Wipe & evidence:
- Deletion process: (1) mark tenant objects deleted, (2) expire/all snapshots & purge metadata, (3) schedule block-level zeroing of blobs, (4) remove references and rotate any associated ephemeral keys.
- Evidence artifacts: we can provide (a) a deletion event log (timestamped events + requestor), (b) snapshot identifiers removed, and (c) a signed deletion certificate/attestation. I've attached our ops playbook: residency-ops-playbook.pdf and a snapshot procedure doc.

KMS / BYOK:
- BYOK supported. If you provision keys in your KMS and grant Redwood the minimum wrapping/unwrapping permissions, we never store your plaintext or key material. If you destroy the key, ciphertext becomes unrecoverable. We'll provide guidance on key rotation and rewrap flows.

Timeline:
- Typical timelines: logical delete within minutes; purge initiation within 24 hours; physical block-scrub completed depending on data size (commonly 24–72 hours for typical tenant sizes). Attestation generation within 48 hours after physical scrub completes. We can negotiate accelerated timelines for high-priority requests.

Next steps:
- Marissa will drop a sample deletion log and a template attestation for your auditors.
- Can we schedule a 30-min ops review this week to walk through the playbook and align on runbook steps for Helios (key lives, snapshot TTLs, and emergency expunge)?

Hi Alice — following up with the technical artifacts Marissa promised. I've uploaded the sample deletion log and an attestation template to the shared drive and attached small samples here. Key notes:

- Sample deletion log (attached as sample-deletion-log.csv): contains columns [timestamp_iso, tenant_id, event_type, object_id, snapshot_id, operator, request_id, checksum_of_deleted_blob]. All timestamps are RFC3339 and the log entries are write-once; we also include a sequence id for immutability when requested.
- Attestation: we can produce a signed PDF attestation that includes tenant id, deletion window, snapshot ids removed, operator identity, and a hash of the deletion log for verifiability. See attached attestation-template.pdf.
- KMS behavior: when BYOK is in use and the key is destroyed by the customer, the ciphertext is irrecoverable. For Redwood-managed keys, we rotate keys on 30/90 day cadence and can provide key lifecycle logs on request.
- Audit reports: we can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II for the Redwood Private control plane; we'll place that in the shared drive and provide a secure link to your procurement team.

Operational suggestion: run a staged "tenant-handback" exercise in a non-prod staging environment where we (1) create a snapshot, (2) perform an expunge request, (3) produce the deletion artifacts, and (4) validate the attestation against the deletion-log hash. This gives Helios a reproducible acceptance test.

Attachments: [Attachment: sample-deletion-log.csv (text/csv)], [Attachment: attestation-template.pdf (application/pdf)]

Happy to run the staging teardown with your infra team next week — suggest Tue/Wed mornings.
